A NERC Category P23 (stuck breaker) contingency of the 41RB7 breaker will clear both Benton County 230/69 kV TR13, the Benton County-Milaca 230 kV line, and open-end both the Benton County-Milaca 69 kV line and Benton County-Liberty 69 kV line at Benton County.  This removes both 230 kV sources into the area 69 kV load pocket and makes the 69 kV circuits radially fed, which can cause voltages to approach or exceed limits.  The breaker station will allow the Liberty substation to support the load pocket for this contingency. 

Loss of the Benton County end of the Benton County-Milaca 69 kV line requires specific reconfiguration to minimize the flicker impact of motors starting at ECE’s Pipeline 2 substation while minimizing Delivery Point exposure.  The breaker station will reduce or eliminate this concern. 

Historical momentary and sustained reliability of the Benton County-Milaca 69 kV line has been poor.   

The reliability risk grade for this circuit is an "F" which is an indication that analysis should be done for enhanced sectionalizing. Enhanced sectionalizing can be achieved by adding motors to switches so they can be operated remotely and/or by adding reclosers or breaker stations. 

The reliability grade for this circuit is a "D" which is an indication that analysis should be done to improve reliability. Frequency of outages is driving the poor grade. A breaker station will reduce the frequency of the substation outages by sectionalizing total exposure and load served. 

This circuit has a summer MW-mile value of 1048 and a winter value of 1136, which, while not extreme, are higher than most circuits.  Adding the breaker station will reduce the exposure to the area East Central Energy (ECE) Delivery Points.

This project will provide looped service to six ECE distribution substations which is needed based on exposure and need to be able to backfeed loads when the main source is lost.

The 69 kV Stinson area loads (Bardon, Amnicon, and Stinson) have a back up source (Fond Du Lac 46/69 kV) which relies on MP’s 46 kV system (23 Line) served between Bear Creek and Thomson H.E.  Minnesota Power has alluded to removing the 23 Line since it is very hard to maintain in the Jay Cooke State Park about 10 years ago and yet to move on the project.  After GRE removes its dependency from the 23 Line, MP can retire the line and GRE can retire Fond Du Lac (S24).

The Fond Du Lac – Summit Tap “DF” 69 kV line (9.92 miles, 2/0 ACSR, 1965) is nearing the end of life and will need rebuilding very soon.  The Dairyland – Summit 69 kV project will remove the dependency on this line and can avoid rebuilding the “DF” line.

The Frog Creek area loads (Wascott, Crystal Lake, and Dairyland) are served from a radial 69 kV system with slight back up from the Dahlberg system (SS-3115).  Connecting to the Dahlberg system has its issues and isn’t an ideal way to back up the Frog Creek area loads.  The Dairyland – Summit 69 kV line will allow for GRE to transfer loads between the Stinson and Frog Creek sources.
